title: Chrono-Anchor Trace Lens: compact, anchored timeline for request drilldown
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Engineers need a compact, scannable way to investigate individual LLM inference requests in the Redwood Console without leaving the performance context (latency, cost, model variant). Current trace UIs scatter spans across long waterfalls making it hard to compare repeated requests, identify systemic vs per-request anomalies, and surface correlation IDs alongside cost and KV cache hits.

Goal: Deliver a lightweight trace drilldown UI (Chrono-Anchor Trace Lens) that anchors a request in time, surfaces correlated spans and metadata, and enables quick triage flows: top-level summary -> focused span comparison -> jump-to-logs / snapshot / replay. Prioritize discoverability for correlation IDs, bucketed latencies, and quick filters (by span kind, model, cache-miss).

Scope: Design a prototype for the Console’s Request Inspector panel: (1) anchored horizontal timeline with per-span compact lanes, (2) correlation-row showing linked requests and downstream effects, (3) foldable span groups (compute/batching/kv/cache/network), (4) dynamic time-slice scrubber that pins the view to a canonical request, (5) inline cost token breakdown popover tied to generation spans, (6) shareable snapshot link and export to incident notes.

Constraints: Must integrate with existing trace ingestion (OpenTelemetry traces + Redwood meta fields), support high-span requests (up to ~120 spans) via virtualization, and preserve Console performance targets (<200ms interactive update for typical slices). Accessibility: keyboard-first navigation between spans and clear focus states for anchors.

Success metrics: reduce mean time-to-detect root cause for request regressions by 30% in pilot accounts; >80% positive usability feedback in design validation sessions; no Console P50 interaction latency regression post-launch.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Maya Patel: Initial kickoff, sketched three layout variants: stacked waterfall, lane-compact, and anchored horizon. Agreed to prototype anchored horizon + scrubber for fastest discovery flow.
2026-02-18 - Liam O'Connor: First interactive Figma screens uploaded. Focused on virtualization strategy notes for 100+ spans. Asked Eng to validate feasibility for inline token-cost popovers.
2026-02-25 - Priya Rao (Eng): Confirmed virtualization approach. Raised concern about many live annotations causing render churn; recommended server-side pre-aggregation for correlation buckets.
2026-03-02 - Noah Kim (PM): Requested inclusion of rollup metric toggles (SLO breaches, p50/p95) and a compact breadcrumbs bar to jump to model variant or region.

2026-03-05 - UsabilityLab: 6-session unmoderated test; participants completed triage tasks 22% faster with anchored timeline vs control. Noted confusion around color encoding for cache-hit vs cache-miss.
2026-03-10 - Design Review: Presented to Eng + PM. Action items: update color legend for cache hits, add explicit correlation ID copy action, wire snapshot export flow to incident template.

2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Iterated prototype addressing feedback and filed follow-up ENG tickets for telemetry changes (ENG-20433) and snapshot URL signing (ENG-20434). Ready for engineering handoff.
review_feedback: 2026-03-03 - Priya Rao (Eng): +1 for compact lanes; ask: include a fallback when KV cache metadata is missing to avoid noisy UIs.
2026-03-05 - Noah Kim (PM): Prefer cost popovers to be optional per-customer (config toggle) to avoid exposing internal pricing to some enterprise customers.
2026-03-10 - Security (Anika Sharma): Snapshot links must be signed and respect Private deployment ACLs. Flagged for engineering (ENG-20434).
decisions: Adopt anchored horizon layout (single canonical request anchor with surrounding correlated requests) as primary default for Request Inspector.
Use banded lanes grouped by semantic span type (Model/Batching/KV/Network) with fold-to-drilldown behavior to manage density.
Expose cost/token breakdown as opt-in per-organization setting; default shown for internal pilots.
Snapshot sharing implemented via signed, time-limited URLs that inherit Console RBAC in Private deployments.
Server-side correlation bucketing will be delivered by Eng to minimize client rendering work (ENG-20433).
